children: New Delhi, Oct. 30 -- The Indian stock market is expected to begin Friday's trading session, October 30, on a subdued note, as indicated by GIFT Nifty. The index was trading near 23,038, down around 15 points or 0.07% from the previous close of Nifty futures, signalling a largely flat opening for domestic benchmark indices.

In the previous session on Thursday, benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty ended firmly in the green, gaining over 1% each, driven by strong buying across banking, FMCG and IT stocks. The 30-share BSE Sensex advanced 905.01 points, or 1.24%, to settle at 74,151.04, marking its highest closing level in over a week. Meanwhile, the NSE Nifty 50 rose 237.90 points, or 1.05%, to end the session at 22,936.75.

Several stocks are likely to remain on investors' radar as companies announce business and corporate developments. Updates related to fresh order wins, operational performance, expansion strategies and other company-specific announcements could drive stock-specific action during Friday's trading session.
Reliance Industries, Jio Platforms, Bharat Electronics, IndiGo, Suzlon Energy, Trent, Vedanta Power, RVNL among shares in focus on Friday.

Shares of Reliance Industries, Jio Platforms, Sun Pharmaceutical Industries, Bharat Electronics, Indian Oil Corporation, Varun Beverages, GAIL will remain in focus as companies are scheduled to release their Q2 results 2026 today.

Tata Group-owned retail company Trent posted a 25.3% year-on-year (YoY) rise in consolidated net profit to Rs.468.09 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs.373.42 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

Suzlon Energy reported a 69% YoY drop in consolidated net profit to Rs.394 crore for the September quarter, against Rs.1,279 crore in Q2 FY26. However, revenue from operations climbed 26% to Rs.4,869 crore, driven by record quarterly wind turbine deliveries of 710 MW.

InterGlobe Aviation, which operates budget airline IndiGo, narrowed its consolidated net loss to Rs.1,879 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs.2,582 crore in the year-ago period. However, the loss widened sequentially from Rs.237 crore reported in the June quarter.

Vedanta Power returned to profitability in the September quarter of FY27, reporting a profit after tax (PAT) of Rs.83 crore against a net loss of Rs.1,688 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. The company had posted a net loss of Rs.423 crore in Q1 FY27.

RVNL has secured a letter of award (LoA) from the Ministry of External Affairs to prepare a detailed project report (DPR) for establishing a Professional and Technical Education Centre (PTEC) in Seychelles.
Vedanta Oil and Gas reported a 21% quarter-on-quarter decline in profit to Rs.746 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs.944 crore in the preceding June quarter.
Promoter Sagility BV is reportedly planning to offload a 12% stake in the company through a block deal valued at Rs.2,377 crore, according to reports.
